target_claim_or_section: §2 G1 (4-12 months) exit criterion '>=2 paying customers' sold to SEG-012/SEG-002/SEG-010
challenge: The G1 clock is inconsistent with the package's own register. market-segments.csv gives 12-24 month sales cycles for SEG-012, SEG-002 and SEG-010 (9-24), the exact segments G1 sells to. Two paying customers within 8 months of G1 start would require cycles shorter than any figure in the register, from a vendor with no references. The SEG-012 basis (announcement to go-live) measures implementation lag, not selection, so even 12-24 is probably a lower bound on time from first contact to PO.
evidence: market-segments.csv SEG-002 12-24, SEG-010 9-24, SEG-012 12-24 months; 11 §2 table; 16 §2 G1 = months 4-12
proposed_change: Re-derive the G1 duration from the register (first PO no earlier than month ~12-18 from first contact). Either extend G1 to 12-24 months and re-cost it, or change the exit criterion to signed LOIs or paid pilots rather than paying customers.

target_claim_or_section: §3 MVEP 'needs ... no SOC 1 reliance at first'
challenge: This mixes up SOC 1 and SOC 2. The wedge needs no SOC 1 report, but the migration assessment ingests donor PII and fund balances, and the evidence feed is a hosted SaaS. Any sponsor with an IT or vendor-risk function, and certainly any administrator or platform buyer, will ask for SOC 2 Type 2 or a security questionnaire plus pen test. A first Type 2 takes about 6-15 months end to end (at least 3 months of observation). Also, if the reconciliation report is used to support opening balances, the sponsor's auditor will rely on it, which is SOC 1 territory. CLM-040 already concedes a 12-24 month SOC gap, but 16 does not carry it into the wedge timeline or cost.
evidence: CLM-040 (claims.csv); 11 §3 last bullet; Drata/Scrut/Bastion SOC 2 timelines 6-15 months, >=3-month observation (vendor sources, may be optimistic); SEG-009 compliance = SOC 2 + DPA
proposed_change: Add a SOC 2 Type 1 at G0 and a Type 2 window starting in G1 as gating items, with cost (~$30-100k first year incl. tooling, ASSUMPTION) and lead time. State plainly that before Type 2 the only buyers are those willing to accept a questionnaire and a bridge letter, and size that subset.

target_claim_or_section: §2/§3 vendor financial viability (G1 capital $0.7-1.2M; CLM-028 wedge never cash-positive)
challenge: Under the 2023 interagency TPRM guidance, a bank or trust buyer reviews the vendor's financial condition, usually from audited statements. The package's own models say the wedge is not cash-positive in more than 99% of ER-2 draws and needs $4-7M to reach the licensing break-even. A diligence analyst reading those numbers would flag going-concern risk and ask for source-code escrow, step-in or transition rights, and a parent guarantee or larger insurance. The 12 §4 remedy (prepaid implementation, minimum fees) also runs against buyer behaviour: buyers refuse to prepay an undercapitalised vendor because the prepayment is itself credit exposure.
evidence: Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships (88 FR 37920, 2023-06-09): financial condition is a due-diligence factor (audited financials); CLM-028; 14 §1 MD-6 $4-7M; 12 §4
proposed_change: Add a 'vendor viability package' requirement (audited financials or committed funding letter, escrow, transition-assistance clause) to G1, and drop prepaid implementation as the concentration remedy for institutional buyers, or show a buyer that has accepted it.

target_claim_or_section: §3 bundle 'migration assessment + charity eligibility evidence feed' as one buyable unit
challenge: Procurement would treat these as two purchases with different budget owners and contract types. The assessment is a one-time professional-services SOW from the CFO/COO project budget during re-platforming. The evidence feed is a recurring SaaS or data licence owned by grants compliance and needs a full security review, data-licence terms and an SLA. Bundling them pushes the cheap SOW through the heavier SaaS review and lengthens the cycle. There is also a conflict of interest: a sponsor in a re-platforming window is choosing a destination platform, which usually includes migration (doc 08: free migration is table stakes, CLM-021). An 'independent' assessment from a vendor that wants to become the platform will be discounted, or excluded from the RFP under independence rules.
evidence: 08 §1 'Free migration offers ... Table stakes (CLM-021)'; 08 §6 'no direct evidence'; 16 §3; CLM-016 (switches go to integrated suites)
proposed_change: Price-test the two components separately in V-2/V-8 and record budget owner and contract vehicle for each. Add a test of whether sponsors will buy an assessment from a non-destination vendor, and whether that disqualifies the vendor from the subsequent RFP.

target_claim_or_section: §3 pre-signature steps 4-5 (local profiler in sponsor environment; NDA only)
challenge: Running vendor code inside the sponsor's environment is not 'NDA only'. It is a software-installation event that needs IT security review, change control and often a signed MSA, which is the same paperwork the step is meant to avoid. Sending k-suppressed aggregates also gives little protection at community-foundation scale (median 46 DAFs per SEG-002): fund-type counts and null rates for 46 funds can identify individuals. And the incumbent agreement (confidential report formats, benchmark clauses, which 08 notes but does not resolve) may forbid sharing schema or exports with a competitor before notice is given. V-4 in doc 22 says 'under NDA', but 08 §3 says real records need a DPA, so the two documents contradict each other.
evidence: 08 §3 'Not possible before signature without a data processing agreement'; 22 V-4 'One sponsor export under NDA'; 12 SEG-002 median 46 DAFs; 08 §3 constraint list (benchmark clauses)
proposed_change: Recast pre-contract work as 'paid T2 under MSA + DPA' rather than NDA. Set a minimum fund count below which no aggregates leave the sponsor. Make incumbent-contract review a precondition before any profiler runs, and fix the NDA/DPA wording in V-4.

target_claim_or_section: §1 table 'External dependence: Channel partner; hosting' (MD-6 and shared infrastructure rows)
challenge: The dependency list leaves out what a vendor-risk questionnaire asks about first: the cloud host and region, the LLM/AI provider (08 §1 relies on LLM mapping suggestions applied to sponsor data), and any data sources or subcontractors behind the evidence feed. Each is a subprocessor that must be disclosed. Donor data sent to an AI API needs DPA flow-down, no-training terms and buyer approval, and many banks require a fourth-party inventory and concentration review. The core migration engine (Transitus) is an unmerged, provisional PR (08 header), so the product being sold depends on code that does not exist on the main branch yet.
evidence: 08 header 'PR #1 not merged, provisional'; 08 §1 'LLM/ML mapping suggestions'; 14 §1 dependence column; interagency guidance on subcontractor oversight (88 FR 37920)
proposed_change: Add a subprocessor register (hosting, AI model provider, data sources, payment, email) with DPA, no-training and data-residency terms. Define an AI-off mode for buyers who ban external LLMs. Treat Transitus maturity as a G0 dependency.

target_claim_or_section: §1 'Liability / insurance: E&O; media rider' for charity intelligence and shared infrastructure
challenge: The insurance and liability exposure is understated. If an eligibility feed wrongly marks a charity as eligible, the sponsor may make a grant that is a taxable expenditure (IRC 4966) or an OFAC breach, and buyers will ask the vendor to indemnify that and to accept higher liability caps for data and confidentiality breaches. A migration reconciliation error that misstates opening balances is a professional-liability event. Typical buyer requirements are cyber cover of several million dollars, E&O, breach notification within 24-72 hours, audit rights and subcontractor flow-down. A $0.7-1.2M company may not be able to buy that cover at those limits, and the premiums are not in the capital estimates.
evidence: 14 §1 liability column; 16 §2 G1 capital $0.7-1.2M; SEG-009 compliance 'SOC 2, DPA'; 12 §3 eligibility service route
proposed_change: Add a contract-terms register (liability cap, indemnities, insurance limits, breach SLA, audit rights) with premiums costed into G1. Disclaim eligibility determinations explicitly (evidence, not determination) and test whether buyers accept that disclaimer in V-8.

target_claim_or_section: §2 'PR #88 and PR #86 used $125k per sponsor (ASSUMPTION)' and 22 G0 cost lines
challenge: The $125k CAC is untested, and the validation budget understates acquisition labour. Ten structured win/loss interviews with sponsors that switched ($5-20k) and five channel-partner conversations leading to a term sheet ($5-15k) leave nothing for senior founder time, travel, conference presence or legal review of a term sheet. A channel partner will also run its own vendor diligence on the entrant before it signs. With 12-24 month cycles, founder-led selling and a low close rate on a two-customer pipeline, fully loaded CAC for the first institutional customers is plausibly several times $125k. Section 22 also cuts acquisition cost by treating the assessment as pipeline ('value is pipeline and evidence, not margin'), so the same activity is counted as both revenue and CAC reduction.
evidence: 11 §2; 22 §1 V-1, V-6 costs; 08 §6 'value is pipeline and evidence'; SEG-001 cac_evidence 'founder-led, one long cycle per deal'
proposed_change: Build a bottom-up CAC (founder FTE-months × cycle length ÷ expected close rate, plus security and legal response costs) and run sensitivity at 2× and 4× $125k through ER-2/ER-4. Count assessment margin and CAC once, not both.

target_claim_or_section: §2 G2 licensed platform via bank/trust distributor (12-36 months)
challenge: Bank and trust distribution needs the distributor's TPRM approval and then each bank's. Banks are rated 5/5 complexity in doc 11, with 6-24 month cycles and a SOC 2 Type 2 requirement that the entrant lacks for 12-24 months (CLM-040). If the SOC clock starts at G1 (month ~4-12), the first clean Type 2 arrives around months 16-28, and the bank cycle comes on top of that. A first bank go-live inside 36 months is therefore at the edge of possibility. SEI already chose TIFIN, and the distributor pool is named but unverified ('partner status unknown'). The 30k licensed-account break-even through this channel has no supporting evidence.
evidence: 11 §2 SEG-003 5/5, 6-24 months; CLM-040; 11 §3 'FIS/Fiserv wealth units; partner status unknown'; 12 SEG-003 'SEI already chose TIFIN'
proposed_change: Sequence G2 timelines as SOC Type 2 date + distributor diligence + bank cycle. Drop banks and trusts from G2 unless a named distributor reaches term-sheet stage, and model G2 on CF-software and administrator channels only.

target_claim_or_section: §2 invalidation trigger 6 'slower than one customer a year'
challenge: The kill threshold is too lenient to protect capital. One customer a year at about $15-25k (V-8 bar $15k per year; V-2 bar $25k subscription) never covers G1 burn. The package already concedes that the first customer is more than 25% of revenue for years, and buyer TPRM penalises vendor concentration. The trigger should be set on revenue and reference quality (for example, at least one referenceable institutional customer with a completed security review by month X), because references are the procurement gate.
evidence: 22 §2 item 6; 22 V-2, V-8 thresholds; 12 §4 concentration; CLM-040
proposed_change: Replace the trigger with one tied to time and references: no referenceable customer that has passed a security review by month 18 means pause the thesis. Track security-questionnaire pass rate as a leading indicator.

target_claim_or_section: §2 G0 exit 'or >=3 sponsors in a contract-end window willing to run a T1 assessment' (T0-T1 free per 08 §6)
challenge: A free, no-commitment T1 measures curiosity, not willingness to buy. It also contains a hidden gate: T1 needs the profiler installed in the sponsor environment (see the NDA/privacy row), so even a 'willing' sponsor may be blocked by its own IT. The G0 exit can be passed without any evidence of procurement viability.
proposed_change: Require at least one paid T2 or a signed MSA as the G0 exit, or count only sponsors whose IT has approved the profiler.
